patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and PrestaShop share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than PrestaShop's shape. Choose PrestaShop only if your buying job matches “Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 1” rather than Medusa's shape. Workflow advantage: Medusa leans shared coverage; PrestaShop leans catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and PrestaShop share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax.; PrestaShop is Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 14-day trial; Enterprise quote. WooCommerce keeps t.
- Company-size focus: Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs PrestaShop (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Medusa-leaning — vs PrestaShop-leaning catalog-management.
- Researched limits: Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; PrestaShop — Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free.

Limitations — Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce); PrestaShop: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; POS / omnichannel is module-dependent, not a native retail bundle.

Poor-fit cases: Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · PrestaShop is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free · Avoid Medusa if you actually need PrestaShop's motion (Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. V)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
